Zod objects default to strip behavior, so when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, parse succeeds with only access_token (and the bogus key), dropping expiry_date/refresh_token; the code then overwrites refresh_token with the literal 'refresh_token', corrupting credentials saved via prisma.credential.update. A real defect introduced by this diff

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed property names are evaluated immediately to a single string (whatever `toString()` returns for a Zod type, often effectively a constant like `"[object Object]"`), so they do not act as a catchall/dynamic key matcher. As a result, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, `safeParse(response)` will only accept/retain `access_token` (and at most one oddly-named fixed property), and because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in` and other token response fields can be dropped/ignored rather than validated/preserved. This matches the finding’s core claim that the schema is effectively a no-op for arbitrary token fields.
